fixes.explanation: Not quite, friend. The LORD says He “…alone stretched out the heavens…” (Isaiah 44:24). He also says He spread out the earth “by Myself.” I need a whole crew of bakers to fill my cookie boxes, so the word “alone” makes my mustache drop.

No helpers on this one, baker. The LORD says He “…alone stretched out the heavens, who by Myself spread out the earth…” That means He did it all Himself. I need bakers to fill all my cookie boxes, so I'm impressed.

That's it, baker! The LORD says He “…foils the signs of false prophets and makes fools of diviners…” (Isaiah 44:25). He also “…confounds the wise and turns their knowledge into nonsense…” Their signs and their knowledge don't get them anywhere. Me, I can't even predict when my own timer will go off, so I'll stick with the Word.

It's the opposite, friend. The LORD says He “…foils the signs of false prophets and makes fools of diviners…” He doesn't honor them. He also “…confounds the wise and turns their knowledge into nonsense…” Honoring and rewarding aren't in the verse.

Abandoned is not what the LORD says. He says Jerusalem “…will be inhabited…” and the cities of Judah “…will be rebuilt, and I will restore their ruins…” Rebuilt and restored are the words He uses. Abandoned never shows up in the verse.
It goes the other direction, friend. The LORD doesn't say the currents will rise. He says, “…I will dry up your currents…” Drying up is the opposite of rising.

You got it. The LORD says of Cyrus, king of Persia (Ezra 1:1), “My shepherd will fulfill all that I desire…” Cyrus is a king, and the LORD still calls him a shepherd. I think that's a title worth hearing.
Close, but the LORD doesn't use that word for Cyrus. Cyrus is king of Persia (Ezra 1:1), and the LORD says of him, “My shepherd will fulfill all that I desire…” The title is shepherd.
Priest isn't the word here. The LORD says of Cyrus, king of Persia (Ezra 1:1), “My shepherd will fulfill all that I desire…” Shepherd is the title He gives.

Right on. The LORD says of Jerusalem, “She will be rebuilt…” and of the temple, “Let its foundation be laid.” The city and the temple are both named in the same verse. For the temple, the word He uses is foundation.

Yes. The LORD tells Cyrus, king of Persia (Ezra 1:1), that He has grasped his right hand “…to subdue nations before him…” The verse goes on to say it is also to disarm kings and to open the doors before him. Nations, kings and doors are all in the picture.

That's the one. The LORD says to Cyrus, “I will go before you and level the mountains; I will break down the gates of bronze and cut through the bars of iron.” Level, break down and cut through are all what He says He will do. He is the One who goes before.

The verse doesn't send any army ahead of Cyrus. The LORD says, “I will go before you and level the mountains…” He's the One who goes first. He also says, “I will break down the gates of bronze and cut through the bars of iron.”

That's the word. The LORD gives Cyrus, king of Persia (Ezra 1:1), those hidden riches “…so that you may know that I am the LORD, the God of Israel, who calls you by name.” The treasure points to who is giving it. Knowing Him is the point.

Good guess, friend, but fear isn't the word here. The LORD gives Cyrus, king of Persia (Ezra 1:1), the riches “…so that you may know that I am the LORD, the God of Israel, who calls you by name.” The word is know. Don't sweat it, baker.
Announce isn't there, friend. The LORD gives Cyrus, king of Persia (Ezra 1:1), the riches “…so that you may know that I am the LORD…” The word is know. The verse is about what Cyrus may know.

Persia isn't named as the reason, friend. The LORD says, “For the sake of Jacob My servant and Israel My chosen one, I call you by name…” Those are His own people, and they're the ones He names. Good guess, though, because Persia is where Cyrus sits.

Not this time, baker. The LORD says to Cyrus, king of Persia (Ezra 1:1), “I have given you a title of honor, though you have not known Me.” So when the title was given, Cyrus had not known Him. That makes this one False.

You've got it. The LORD says to Cyrus, king of Persia (Ezra 1:1), “I have given you a title of honor, though you have not known Me.” That means Cyrus had not known Him when the title was given. So False is right.

Whoa, hold on, baker, it's the opposite! The LORD says, “Let the earth open up that salvation may sprout and righteousness spring up with it…” Closed is the one thing the earth is not told to be. And nothing in the verse says to wait for the rain to stop.

Yes, baker. The LORD says Cyrus will rebuild His city and set His exiles free, “…but not for payment or reward, says the LORD of Hosts.” No invoice comes with it. Payment and reward are the two things the verse rules out.

Temple gold isn't named in this verse, friend. The LORD says Cyrus will rebuild His city and set His exiles free, “…but not for payment or reward…” The verse says not for payment or reward, so a share of gold doesn't fit.

No land deal is named in this verse, friend. The LORD says Cyrus will rebuild His city and set His exiles free, “…but not for payment or reward, says the LORD of Hosts.” The verse says not for payment or reward, so land in exchange doesn't fit.
